A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cost for developing software can be kept at an acceptable level by a well planned software development strategy, but that the cost for maintaining the software will increase as a consequence.
the accumulation process is very sensitive to the initial development of software, but less sensitive to the development of software in later years.
we have developed models for software accumulation and have shown that the models are useful for analyzing the impact of different strategic choices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
software development and maintenance should be considered as a whole, rather than separately.
the cost of software maintenance is not a constant fraction of the development cost, but increases over time as the amount of software increases.
software accumulation can be described by simple models, and that the models provide a good framework for understanding the effects of different strategies for software development and maintenance.
